degrade_records.detail: The candidate claims `doc.CreateStructTree()` builds (idempotently) a `/StructTreeRoot` and marks the document Tagged. (+1 identical findings merged)

The candidate claims `doc.AutoTag(opts?)` infers a `/StructTreeRoot` for an untagged document from page layout: headings by font-size clustering (the modal size is body text; larger distinct sizes rank `H1`..`H6`), paragraphs, and images as `Figure` (with `/Alt` from `opts.alt`) or `/Artifact` when undescribed. (+2 identical findings merged)

The candidate claims that `doc.ValidatePdfUa(part?)` checks a curated, machine-checkable subset of PDF/UA-1 (ISO 14289-1) and reports missing or wrong PDF/UA identification (`pdfuaid:part`) at BOTH parts, as a WARNING rather than an error — the reference profile tags every identification rule `minor`, so a document whose only defect is a missing claim still reports `Passed`.

PDF/A validation — `doc.ValidatePdfA(level)` checks a curated, machine-decidable subset of PDF/A (ISO 19005) for parts 1–3 at every conformance level (`'1b'`/`'1a'`/`'2b'`/`'2u'`/`'2a'`/`'3b'`/`'3u'`/`'3a'`): no encryption, file `/ID` present, version ceiling, no external streams or prohibited filters (LZW everywhere; JPX/JBIG2 in part 1), no PostScript/reference XObjects, conformant identification XMP (`pdfaid:part`/`conformance`) and `/Info`↔XMP consistency, a PDF/A `/OutputIntent` whose ICC `/DestOutputProfile` is a profile of the device space the content act (+15 identical findings merged)

Table extraction: tagged `/Table` tree first, else geometry — for a tagged PDF, `GetTables` uses the `/Table → TR → TH/TD` structure tree as the authoritative source for rows/cells/spans (`options.structure = 'off'` forces geometry). Otherwise it reconstructs tables from horizontal/vertical ruling lines and text position, axis-aligned or rotated. The ruled path needs at least one *interior* rule: a bare rectangle outline yields a 1×1 grid, which is page furniture rather than a one-cell table, and is not reported (this also keeps it out of `AutoTag`'s structure tr (+7 identical findings merged)

Stream decoding covers the byte filters; `Save({ streamFilter })` re-filters — decoding supports `FlateDecode`, `LZWDecode`, `ASCII85Decode`, `ASCIIHexDecode`, `RunLengthDecode`, and `BrotliDecode` (with predictors and multi-filter chains), plus `DCTDecode` (baseline/progressive/arithmetic/lossless/hierarchical JPEG), `CCITTFaxDecode` (Group 3 1D/2D and Group 4), `JPXDecode` (JPEG 2000, to 8-bit samples), and `JBIG2Decode` (arithmetic generic/symbol/text + MMR, to 1-bit samples) at the image layer. Matching **encoders** (`ascii85Encode`, `asciiHexEncode`, `lzwEnc (+1 identical findings merged)

HTML export` — `ToHtml` ships both `mode: 'semantic'` (reflowable) and `mode: 'fixed'` (visual reproduction with absolutely positioned text over a vector or raster backdrop). A raster backdrop is a second pass through the rasterizer, so a raster-backed page costs one extra interpretation of its content and produces a much larger file than the vector default; `backdropScale` is the only lever on its size, since exposing width/height would let the raster's aspect ratio diverge from the page's. With `forms: true`, field values are exported as control values, so a ** (+4 identical findings merged)

Hyphenation — nine bundled languages (no Russian: its patterns are LPPL-only); a drawn hyphen is page content, so extracted text reads `hyu00ADnphen` (a soft hyphen, from a Standard-14 face) or `hy-nphen` (an embedded font, which has no second code for the glyph), and it is not marked as an artifact or given `/ActualText`; HTML `hyphens`, headings and code blocks do not hyphenate, and `ReplaceText({ adjust: 'reflow' })` hyphenates only when asked (`hyphenate`); a table column's auto-fit width still assumes whole words; soft hyphens in text that does NOT ask for hyphenation still draw as WinAno

Tab stops — no bar tabs and no list-number tabs (DOCX import reports both); table cells take no tab stops — a tab in an authored cell draws nothing, and one in a DOCX cell is drawn as a space and reported; a stop is measured from the block's left edge, so a stop past the right edge is never reached and the tab ends its line; tabs cannot be combined with `shape: true`; Markdown and HTML carry no tab stops.
A note reference inside another note (Word never writes one) (+2 identical findings merged)

There is **no oracle for the rendering**: the reader beneath it is checked against Word 2010 and LibreOffice on a vendored corpus and the spacing rule against Word through COM, while where the ink lands is held by hand-built cases. (+2 identical findings merged)
Acrobat's tab-delimited content is reproduced from rules read off Adobe Reader 26.1's own script engine, so it is evidence from one producer and one version. (+1 identical findings merged)
Reader neither recomputes nor draws these barcodes: Acrobat's script needs an object Reader lacks, so the value becomes a single space there.

Footnotes and endnotes — Flow only: a note reference in a table cell, a floating box or a CSS float is refused with an error, and so is one reaching a single-rect placement (`page.AddHtml`, `page.AddDocx`, `placeElements`); `page.AddMarkdown` places its notes after the content instead. (+2 identical findings merged)

A symbolic font (Wingdings, Symbol) that states no encoding is embedded from a face with a (3,0) symbol cmap and stays a symbolic `/TrueType`, its codes reaching glyphs through that cmap. (+4 identical findings merged)

The candidate claims that `doc.ValidatePdfX` checks a curated, machine-decidable subset of PDF/X (ISO 15930) at `'1a'` / `'3'` / `'4'` / `'4p'`, and that it returns the same `ValidationReport` as `ValidatePdfA`. However, the facts do not support the existence of `ValidatePdfX` or `ConvertToPdfX` methods, nor do they confirm that these methods return a `ValidationReport` identical to `ValidatePdfA`.

The candidate states that `doc.ConvertToPdfX(level, opts?)` returns a `ConversionReport` (`applied` / `unresolved` / `passed`) and that after the passes it re-runs `ValidatePdfX(level)`, so `unresolved`/`passed` exactly mirror the validator. However, the facts do not support the existence of `ConvertToPdfX`, nor do they confirm the structure of its return value or that it internally calls `ValidatePdfX`.

XFA converts to AcroForm, with limited content splitting — `doc.ConvertXfaToAcroForm()` reads an `/AcroForm /XFA` packet (single-stream XDP or the alternating name/stream array), models the `template` packet's field set, binds values out of `datasets`, and emits a real `/AcroForm` field tree; `/XFA` and the catalog's `/NeedsRendering` are then removed by default. (+13 identical findings merged)

Image insertion is JPEG, PNG, BMP and TIFF — `AddImage` accepts JPEG (`DCTDecode`, including CMYK), PNG (`FlateDecode`, including interlaced/Adam7 and palette `tRNS`), BMP and TIFF (both decoded to samples and stored as `FlateDecode`; the saved file carries no trace of the original container). (+3 identical findings merged)

units.text: Aspose.PDF FOSS for TypeScript reads and writes PDF documents, converts them to HTML, Markdown, DOCX, EPUB, TIFF, and SVG, and supports page inspection, editing, and redaction. It parses a PDF into an in-memory object model on Open, lets mutations act directly on that live model, and serializes a fresh, renumbered document on Save. It also supports document recovery, validation, repair, optimization, signing, and encryption.

It opens PDFs from files or byte arrays using Document.Open and Document.OpenFile, supports recovery of damaged files with Document.recovery, validates page trees via Document.Validate, repairs issues with Document.Repair, and saves documents synchronously or asynchronously with Document.Save and Document.SaveAsync, while also allowing writes to streams via Document.WriteTo.

It exposes every page through Document.Pages, lets users set page boundaries with Page.Rect, rotate pages with Page.Rotate, access resources and contents via Page.Resources and Page.Contents, and add text, text blocks, images, and tables to pages using Page.AddText, Page.AddTextBlock, Page.AddImage, and Page.AddTable.

It builds flow documents with Flow.AddParagraph, Flow.AddHeading, Flow.AddList, Flow.AddImage, Flow.AddFloatBox, Flow.AddFloatingBox, and Flow.AddTable, and supports adding tables, text, and text blocks directly to pages with Page.AddTable, Page.AddText, and Page.AddTextBlock.

It imports HTML, Markdown, and DOCX content into documents and pages using Document.AddHtml, Document.AddMarkdown, Document.AddDocx, Page.AddHtml, Page.AddMarkdown, Page.AddDocx, and Flow.AddHtml, Flow.AddMarkdown, Flow.AddDocx, with asynchronous variants Flow.AddHtmlAsync and Flow.AddMarkdownAsync.

It creates and edits annotations with Annotation.constructor, sets their rectangle, color, contents, flags, print, hidden, opacity, subtype, and name properties, and manages annotations on pages via Page.Annotations.

It redacts content by rectangle or text search with Page.Redact, Page.RedactText, Document.Redact, and Document.RedactText, marks redactions with Page.MarkRedactText and Document.MarkRedactText, applies them with Page.ApplyRedactions and Document.ApplyRedactions, sanitizes documents with Document.Sanitize, and optimizes them with Document.Optimize and Document.OptimizeAsync.

It signs and certifies documents with Document.Sign and Document.Certify, adds timestamps with Document.AddDocumentTimestamp, includes validation data via Document.AddValidationData, verifies signatures and timestamps with Document.VerifySignatures and Document.VerifyDocumentTimestamps, and manages encryption with EncryptOptions and SignOptions.

It renders pages to SVG with Page.ToSvg, to raster images with Page.ToImage and Page.ToImageAsync, exports pages to Markdown with Page.ToMarkdown and Page.ToMarkdownAsync, exports pages to DOCX with Page.ToDocx, and exports entire documents to HTML, Markdown, DOCX, EPUB, and TIFF with Document.ToHtml, Document.ToMarkdown, Document.ToDocx, Document.ToEpub, and Document.ToTiff.

Aspose.PDF FOSS for TypeScript provides the Document class as the primary entry point for working with PDF documents, offering methods to open, save, and manipulate pages and content. The Document class exposes a Pages collection that provides Page instances for per-page operations.
The Document class supports opening PDFs from bytes or files, saving to disk or memory, validating, repairing, sanitizing, optimizing, signing, and certifying documents.
The Document class provides AddHtml, AddMarkdown, and AddDocx methods to insert content from HTML, Markdown, and DOCX sources into a document.
The Pages collection exposes Page instances with constructors, access to the parent Document, Rect, Rotate, Resources, Contents, and Annotations, plus methods to add text, text blocks, and images.
The Flow class enables multi-column layout authoring with paragraphs, headings, lists, images, tables, and floating boxes, supporting hyphenation, tab stops, and complex-text shaping.
The Annotation class represents annotations with Rect, Color, Contents, Flags, Print, Hidden, Opacity, Subtype, and Name properties, accessible via Page.Annotations.
Redaction functionality is available through Document.Redact, Page.Redact, and related methods to mark and apply redactions, redact text by search, and sanitize documents.
Document signing and certification are supported via Document.Sign, Document.Certify, and methods to add timestamps and validation data, with options for encryption and signature appearance.
Export functionality converts documents and pages to DOCX, SVG, TIFF, HTML, Markdown, and EPUB formats, supporting both reflowed and fixed-layout outputs.
Table authoring is provided through createTable, Page.AddTable, and Flow.AddTable, with BorderInfo, CellBuilder, CellOptions, and CellTextOptions for styling.
Flow supports adding HTML content via AddHtml and AddMarkdown methods, with async variants available for non-blocking authoring.
Flow authoring includes AddParagraph, AddHeading, AddList, AddImage, AddFloatBox, AddFloatingBox, and AddTable methods for structured content.
Flow provides async variants of AddHtml and AddMarkdown to support non-blocking HTML and Markdown rendering into multi-column layouts.
It adds broader proprietary-format support, rendering, and advanced document-processing capabilities this FOSS build leaves unimplemented.

Signer class represents a signer.
SkippedFont class holds baseFont and reason members.
SkippedFrame class holds frame and reason members; frame is the 0-based index in the source file and reason is the decoder's own message.

SplitOptions class holds preserveStructure and prunePolicy members; preserveStructure specifies whether to preserve the source's tagged structure tree and prunePolicy specifies the pruning policy applied while extracting each page's object graph.

StampWithOptions class holds mode, opacity, rect, and rotate members; mode specifies whether to draw on top or behind existing content, opacity sets constant opacity 0..1, rect sets the target box the source is fitted into, and rotate sets extra clockwise rotation of the placed content in degrees.
StdFont class represents a standard font.
StreamFilterName class represents a stream filter name.

SummarizeOptions class holds instructions, maxInputChars, pages, and signal members; instructions specifies how the summary should read, maxInputChars sets characters per request, and pages specifies pages to summarize.
SummarizeResult class holds requests, text, and usage members; requests lists model calls made and usage is summed across requests when reported.
SvgOptions class holds annotations and box members; annotations specifies composite annotation and form-field /AP appearances and box specifies which page box defines the viewport.
SyncDirection class represents a synchronization direction.
TabAlign class represents a tab alignment.
TabLeader class represents a tab leader.
TableAttributes class holds colSpan, headers, rowSpan, scope, and summary members.
TableStitchOptions class holds the stitch member, which merges continuations across page boundaries.

Template class provides PlaceOn, constructor, and page members; PlaceOn draws this template onto page inside rect [x, y, w, h] and constructor is internal, for use with Document.NewTemplate; PlaceOn throws TypeError conditionally.

TextAnnotation class provides Author, Color, Contents, Flags, Flatten, Hidden, AddReply, and AddStateReply members; AddReply creates a /Text reply on this annotation's page and AddStateReply appends a state record, while AddReply and AddStateReply throw TypeError conditionally.

TextBlockOptions class holds align, atomics, breakAnywhere, defaultTabInterval, firstLineIndent, hyphenate, leading, and rotate members; align specifies horizontal alignment of each line, atomics specifies boxes to place among the runs, breakAnywhere is internal for plain-text import, and defaultTabInterval sets points between implicit stops past the last explicit one.

TextChange class holds new, newText, old, oldText, and op members; new specifies where newText lies, newText is the text on the second document's side, old specifies where oldText lies, and oldText is the text on the first document's side.

TextComparison class holds changes, granularity, minimal, pages, and stats members; changes lists every run in reading order, granularity specifies what a token was and how runs join, minimal is false when the search budget cut a comparison short, and pages lists one entry per page pair in pages mode.
TextComparisonStats class holds newTokens, oldTokens, and similarity members; oldTokens counts words compared in the first document.

TextFont class holds bold, canEncode, codeWidth, constructor, decode, decodeGlyphs, decodeRun, and dict members; bold indicates whether the document declares this font bold or italic, codeWidth specifies the narrowest character code this font admits, decode decodes a show-string's bytes into Unicode text, and decodeGlyphs decodes bytes into one record per character code; encode throws UnsupportedFeatureError conditionally.
TextFragment class holds the text content, baseline angle, font name, font size, and page-space axis box of a text fragment.
TextLine class holds the text, page-space bounding box, fragments, and styles of a text line.
TextSpan class holds the text and 1-based page number of a text span.
TextWatermark class holds the kind and first occurrence's text of a text watermark.
TiffEncodeOptions class holds the compression setting, default 'deflate'.
TimeStampRequestInfo class holds the hash algorithm, imprint, and nonce of a timestamp request.
TimeStampRequestOptions class holds the certificate request flag, anti-replay nonce, and request policy OID.
TimeStampTokenOptions class holds the generation time, policy, and serial number of a timestamp token.
TimestampInfo class holds whether the token's message imprint matches, the TSA policy OID, the token serial number, and the TSA-asserted signing time.
TimestampProvider class provides timestamping functionality.
TransitionDirection class represents transition direction values.
TstInfo class holds the generation time, hash algorithm, imprint, nonce, policy, and serial number of a timestamp token info.
UnreflowableText class holds the first match in the paragraph, 1-based page number, and reason for unreflowable text.
UnsupportedFeatureError class is raised when an unsupported feature is encountered.
ValidationDataOptions class holds the extra certificates, CRL retrieval, and OCSP retrieval settings.
VectorGraphics class provides methods to draw vector graphics and manage marked-content sequences and layers, where arc, roundedRect, setDash, and setMiterLimit throw TypeError conditionally.
ViewerPreferences class holds the center window flag, predominant reading order, document title display flag, and duplex printing setting.
ViewerPreferencesUpdate class represents an update to viewer preferences.
WatermarkCandidate class represents a watermark candidate.
XfaConvertOptions class holds the remove XFA flag.
XfaConvertReport class holds the chrome pages, XDP packets, and skipped items of an XFA conversion.
XfaFieldResult class holds the SOM path and 1-based page number of an XFA field.
XfaSkipped class holds the SOM path for a field and the reason for skipping.
XmpValueInput class holds the alt, bag, lang, seq, struct, and uri flags for XMP value input.
XmpWriteOptions class holds the prefix to write the namespace under.
